scope: matched language-conditioned MiniMax-H3 robot-action generation from one real-scene video
summary: Three 124-frame MiniMax-H3 outputs completed from the same real source video with different insert, handover, and inspect prompts, but the full video reference dominated motion and the action variants remained visually near-identical.
evidence: outputs/minimax-h3-action-control/20260810T045600Z-flower-actions-v1/metadata.json records three completed and decoded NF4 H3 outputs on physical A800 GPU 7
The five-round comparison manifest measured a post-repair pairwise full-frame MAD floor of 1.0615, below the 2.0 distinctness gate
One-second raw contact sheets show nearly the same robot pose progression for insert, handover, and inspect despite different prompt timelines
All three best repairs reached background lock 1.0, object lock 1.0, subject replacement about 0.8997, and robot identity only about 0.6003-0.6009
lessons: MiniMax-H3 Ref2VA full-video conditioning can dominate explicit language motion instructions even when the prompt says not to copy source-human motion.
Pairwise output differences must be visually and semantically inspected; a nonzero pixel MAD is not evidence of action controllability.
limitations: The attempt does not demonstrate precise language action control because the three commanded actions are not visibly separable.
Third-party NF4 weights were used rather than official BF16 MiniMax-H3 weights.
The 5.17-second outputs are image-space generations, not physical robot execution.
next_actions: Remove source temporal motion from the H3 conditioning path by using a real-video scene anchor image, then restore the aligned real source outside the generated subject region and re-evaluate all actions.
